examples.solution_text:
In $\Delta ABD$ and $\Delta CDB$:

$AB=CD$ (given)

$AD=CB$ (given)

$BD$ is common.

$\therefore\Delta ABD\equiv\Delta CDB$ (SSS).

$\angle ADB=\angle CBD$ (corresponding angles in congruent triangles).

$\therefore AD\parallel BC$ (equal alternate angles).

In $\Delta AED$ and $\Delta CEB$:

$AE=CE$ (given)

$\angle AED=\angle CEB$ (vertically opposite angles)

$DE=BE$ (given).

The equal angle is included between the two equal sides.

$\therefore\Delta AED\equiv\Delta CEB$ (SAS).

$\angle EAD=\angle ECB$ (corresponding angles in congruent triangles).

In $\Delta ABC$ and $\Delta EDC$:

$\angle ACB=\angle ECD$ (vertically opposite angles)

$\angle BAC=\angle DEC$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel DE$)

$BC=DC$ (given).

$\therefore\Delta ABC\equiv\Delta EDC$ (AAS).

In $\Delta PSQ$ and $\Delta PSR$:

$\angle PSQ=\angle PSR=90^\circ$ ($PS\perp QR$)

$PQ=PR$ (given hypotenuses)

$PS$ is common.

$\therefore\Delta PSQ\equiv\Delta PSR$ (RHS).

$QS=RS$ (corresponding sides in congruent triangles).

Since $S$ lies on $QR$, $S$ is its midpoint.

In $\Delta AOB$ and $\Delta DOC$:

$OA=OD$ (radii of the same circle)

$\angle AOB=\angle DOC$ (vertically opposite angles)

$OB=OC$ (radii of the same circle).

$\therefore\Delta AOB\equiv\Delta DOC$ (SAS).

$\angle OAB=\angle ODC$ (corresponding angles in congruent triangles).

$\therefore AB\parallel CD$ (equal alternate angles).

In $\Delta OAD$ and $\Delta OBD$:

$OA=OB$ (radii of the same circle)

$AD=BD$ (given)

$OD$ is common.

$\therefore\Delta OAD\equiv\Delta OBD$ (SSS).

$\angle ODA=\angle ODB$ (corresponding angles in congruent triangles).

$\angle ODA+\angle ODB=180^\circ$ (angles on the straight line $AB$).

The angles are equal and sum to $180^\circ$, so each is $90^\circ$.

$\therefore OD\perp AB$.

In $\Delta ABD$ and $\Delta CBD$:

$\angle ABD=\angle CBD=90^\circ$ ($BD\perp AC$)

$\angle ADB=\angle CDB$ (given)

$BD$ is common.

$\therefore\Delta ABD\equiv\Delta CBD$ (AAS).

$AD=CD$ (corresponding sides in congruent triangles).

$\therefore\Delta ACD$ is isosceles (two equal sides).

In $\Delta ABC$ and $\Delta ADC$:

$\angle ABC=\angle ADC=90^\circ$ (given)

$AC$ is the common hypotenuse.

$AB=AD$ (given).

$\therefore\Delta ABC\equiv\Delta ADC$ (RHS).

$\angle BAC=\angle DAC$ (corresponding angles in congruent triangles).

$\therefore AC$ bisects $\angle BAD$.

OA=OB as radii, AD=BD=2 cm and OD is common, establishing OAD≡OBD by SSS. Corresponding angles ODA and ODB are equal and sum to 180° on AB, so each is 90° and OD⊥AB.
Both angles at B are 90°, both stated angles at D are 35°, and BD is common. AAS establishes ABD≡CBD with A↔C. Consequently AD=CD, making ACD isosceles. The remaining angles are both 55°.
The right angles are at B and D, AC is the common hypotenuse, and AB=AD=3 cm. RHS establishes ABC≡ADC. Corresponding angles BAC and DAC are equal, so the interior segment AC bisects ∠BAD.
